text:
I'm receiving my A750 and A770's soon (possibly next week, fingers crossed).

Would GN be interested in receiving some benchmarks comparing a suite of DX11 games on RX580 vs A750/A770 using DXVK (DirectX to Vulkan router DLL which was meant for Linux but is also perfectly operational on Windows)?

From what I saw on the Linux side of things, Intel is on the ball with Vulkan development in the drivers and performance is as expected.

There's barely any reason to not use DXVK even on Windows for DX9/10/11 these days as in most games it gives a performance uplift and it's as simple as dropping the DLL and config file in the games root directory.

In some even so great that a game like Fallout 4 on Ultra ran 75fps 1440p in Crossfire on RX580's back in the day now does 75fps on a single card going through Vulkan instead.

For Intel cards especially, this could be just what's needed as it seems it's specifically legacy DirectX versions (9/10/11) that are badly optimized.


I actually kinda wonder why, if some Linux guys can develop a near 100% compatible DirectX to Vulkan wrapper, they don't just bake something similar into their drivers to not have to waste time on Direct 9/10/11 driver development and just pump everything through Vulkan instead.

Dozens of different departments cutting each others throats and competing against each other, which ends up costing the company as a whole and leading to an inferior product. He thought a company would do well if the employees were competing against each other and the departments competing against each other... and he almost drove them bankrupt. When their management forced engineering to rush, the one thing you should never, under any circumstances, rush, the very predictable (except to management types who don't understand engineering at all) happened - it failed.  10nm couldn't get the yields needed, and they wasted time they didn't have. When Gelsinger took over, there seemed to be hope, but he's proven the job is too much for him.  I really don't think it's his fault, he's very smart, but he's a very smart guy trying to work in an environment of management wonks who see intellectual ability as a handicap rather than an asset. Lisa Su becoming CEO of AMD was a last-ditch move of desperation, at best, as far as management was concerned.
